EverMemOS

Current LoCoMo leaderboard #1

Per paper_leaderboard (extracted from Table 1 via Gemini): 93.05% on LoCoMo, with per-category breakdown 96.67 / 91.84 / 89.72 / 76.04. Compare Hindsight 89.61% (abstract-verified), Backboard 90% (their baseline), Full-Context 89%.

Verification status (2026-05-26): Number is table-extracted, NOT in abstract. Abstract claims "state-of-the-art on memory-augmented reasoning" without a number. Trust level: medium-high (leaderboard quote matches Table 1 row format) but not abstract-verified. Need full PDF read to fully verify.

What we know

From the abstract: self-organizing memory operating system that targets long-horizon reasoning. Consolidates evolving user state across sessions; resolves conflicts. Framed as an "OS" (similar to MemGPT/Letta/MemOS lineage). Authors at EverMind (closed-source).

What we don't know yet

Code not released. The paper is in the leaderboard but we haven't done a deep read. Method details (consolidation algorithm, conflict resolution, retrieval, base model) are not yet extracted.

Why it matters

This sets the LoCoMo bar at 93%. Earlier SOTA claims (e.g. TiMem 75.30%) are now 18pp behind. Anything we publish on LoCoMo needs to engage with this number — either close the gap, or report on a different axis (cost, NoReplay-strict budget, generalization).

Next steps

  • Deep PDF read to extract method (mark this file as needs-review until then)
  • Check whether code/weights ever get released
  • Map their "semantic consolidation" against sleep consolidation — likely related but specifics unknown
